claims.text: The driver told the rider of the reroute in-app before he took it: MSG-05006-003 ("Miss, AYE jam already, I go West Coast Highway can?") was sent at 18:01:46 and read at 18:02:06, and the platform's own trip record places the point of deviation at 18:05:06 — three and a half minutes later. POL-RD-21 requires the rider to be informed by in-app chat before or at the point of deviation, and on a chat log graded COMPLETE at weight 1.0 that requirement is met on the face of the record, not merely asserted by the driver.

POL-RD-21 provides that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is 'agreed', and that acknowledgment is on this log: the rider answered the driver's West Coast Highway question with 'ok' at 18:02:11, before the deviation. The rider's statement filed the next day contests only the driver's reason for the reroute ('the AYE looked clear to me'); it does not deny the message, the fact that it was read, or the 'ok', so the rider's consent to this route stands unrebutted on contemporaneous evidence.

The deviation is measured the way POL-RD-22 requires, from the platform's recorded distances: 14.6 km actual less 12.7 km optimal is 1.90 km, over the 1.0 km tolerance. The driver states that plainly rather than reaching for the GPS trace, which POL-RD-22 excludes as a measuring stick because a sparse trace understates a route's length (the trace here reads 12.318 km). This trip therefore turns on the justification and agreement limbs of POL-RD-24, not on the tolerance rows.

The traffic limb is not closed against the driver. EV-ADVIS-05006-02 is a ROADWORK with Lane 1 closed on Pasir Panjang Road (towards Telok Blangah) near Pasir Panjang Wholesale Centre, valid 09:00-23:00 on 18 August and so overlapping the trip window; its kind is an admissible 'closure' under POL-RD-23, and the derived block leaves its intersection with the recommended route expressly undetermined for the Judge — the corridor the vehicle used rejoined the recommended route at the Keppel Road / Telok Blangah Road junction the trip record itself names. The driver reported the traffic in real time in the same chat log. The driver does not put EV-ADVIS-05006-01 forward as showing congestion: its type is NONE and it is confined to the AYE segment.

On that record this trip falls in row (a) of POL-RD-24 — the rider was informed and agreed, the deviation is over 1 km, and a closure-type advisory overlaps the trip window on the corridor the reroute served — and row (a) awards no refund. The 1.37 SGD was nevertheless taken from the driver's earnings on 19 August 2026 (fare_adjusted, payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED), and the excess distance fare is exactly that figure, 1.90 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.37 SGD. Where the driver is owed money the outcome is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd carrying the same 1.37 SGD (POL-GEN-03); the driver asks for that sum back and nothing more.

If the Judge finds the reroute not traffic-justified, the matrix does not settle the case either: the only row that gives effect to the rider's agreement is row (a), and the only closure-type advisory in the trip window carries an undetermined intersection with the recommended route, so the fact POL-RD-23 turns on — whether a closure or congestion affected the recommended route at the trip time — is not carried by the evidence before the Judge. POL-RD-24 sends a case that fits no row to a human, POL-GEN-26 escalates where a fact a rule needs cannot be established, and POL-RD-25 escalates a route deviation that does not meet its confidence threshold. On that alternative the driver asks that the 1.37 SGD be held for that review rather than left where the interim adjustment put it.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you agree on the shape of the trip; you disagree on whether the detour was justified by traffic, and the evidence decides that against the driver.

Deviation (POL-RD-22): the platform's recorded distances give 14.6 km actual less 12.7 km recommended = 1.90 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance. This is not a within-tolerance case, so rows (c) and (e) of the refund matrix are unavailable.

Traffic justification (POL-RD-23): a reroute is justified only where traffic data that intersects the recommended route shows congestion, an incident or a closure. The advisory covering the recommended route — the AYE towards the City, Clementi Road to Keppel Viaduct (EV-ADVIS-05006-01, valid 17:29–18:59, overlapping the trip) — records no incident, roadwork or closure; its type is NONE and its own derived field marks it as not justifying a reroute. The second advisory (EV-ADVIS-05006-02) is a roadwork, but it sits on Pasir Panjang Road towards Telok Blangah — a road on the route the driver actually took, not on the recommended route (Clementi Avenue 2, AYE, Keppel Road, Wallich Street). I resolve that advisory's open intersection field: it does not intersect the recommended route, so it cannot justify leaving it. The driver's real-time assertion of a jam is not traffic data under POL-RD-23. The reroute is not traffic-justified.

Notification and agreement (POL-RD-21): the driver did inform the rider in-app before deviating (MSG-05006-003 at 18:01:46, read 18:02:06) and the rider acknowledged with 'ok' (MSG-05006-004 at 18:02:11), both before the platform recorded the deviation at 18:05:06. That limb is met. But the rider's agreement is decisive only in row (a) of the refund matrix, which also requires the reroute to be traffic-justified — and it is not.

Refund matrix (POL-RD-24): row (d) applies — not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km — and it refunds the excess distance fare in full. That figure is 1.90 km × 0.72 SGD/km = 1.37 SGD, no surge, and it is exactly the 1.37 SGD already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver on 19 August 2026 (payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED).

Outcome (POL-GEN-03): the driver filed contesting that refund. The rider is owed the 1.37 SGD, so the driver's claim is not supported and the present state stands: NO_ACTION, with both amounts null. Nothing is returned to the driver, and no further sum is refunded to the rider — the 1.37 SGD she holds is the amount the policy requires. No clause in this category produces a referral, so none is added.

The driver's alternative request — hold the sum for review if the reroute is found unjustified — is declined. The facts POL-RD-23 turns on are carried by the two advisories and the trip record, so there is no open question for POL-GEN-26 or POL-RD-24's no-row rule to escalate. Confidence: all eight artifacts are COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the deciding facts (the 1.90 km deviation and the absence of traffic justification) carry full weight (POL-GEN-02). The contested amount is 1.37 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD line, so the ruling is final at any confidence; neither profile carries a fraud flag; POL-RD-25's 0.80 bar is met.
